solutions.title: Simplify the base
solutions.body:
$\frac{\tan^{-1}x}{\tan^{-1}x+x}=\frac{1}{1+\frac{x}{\tan^{-1}x}}$, and $\frac{x}{\tan^{-1}x}\to1$ as $x\to0$, so the base tends to $\frac12$ and the limit is $\frac18$.

**Answer: $\frac18$**

solutions.title: Rationalize
solutions.body:
Multiply by $\frac{1-\sqrt{1-x^2}}{1-\sqrt{1-x^2}}$: $\frac{x^2}{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\frac{x^2(1-\sqrt{1-x^2})}{x^2}=1-\sqrt{1-x^2}$. Then $\int_0^11\,dx=1$ and $\int_0^1\sqrt{1-x^2}dx=\frac\pi4$ (quarter disc), so the integral is $1-\frac\pi4=\frac{4-\pi}4$.

**Answer: $\frac{4-\pi}{4}$**

solutions.title: Differentiate the exponential series
solutions.body:
Starting from $e^x=\sum\frac{x^n}{n!}$, applying $x\frac{d}{dx}$ three times gives $\sum\frac{n^3x^n}{n!}=(x+3x^2+x^3)e^x$. At $x=1$ this is $5e$.

**Answer: $5e$**

solutions.title: Rewrite $n^3$
solutions.body:
$n^3=n(n-1)(n-2)+3n(n-1)+n$, and $\sum\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{n!}=e$, $\sum\frac{n(n-1)}{n!}=e$, $\sum\frac n{n!}=e$. So the sum is $e+3e+e=5e$.

**Answer: $5e$**
